paragraph: The live Fast Forward blend selector now starts with an October 19–Present roast-date period, which was not the newest period when this review was first published. The accessible page also lists several historical Guatemala component pairs together, so it does not reliably prove which percentages belong to an unseen bag. Use the printed roast date to select the matching period and ask the roaster if a precise component breakdown matters; do not copy an old pair into a new lot. The medium, nutty-and-sweet brief remains the roaster's intent, not a Coffeedant tasting of the new period. Checked October 21, 2026. [SOURCE]
sourceTitle: Counter Culture Fast Forward dated blend selector
sourceNote: October 19–Present is the newest visible period; accessible text does not bind displayed historic percentages to a delivered bag.

paragraph: For Gradient, Counter Culture's current recipe panel gives two distinct filter starting points: an automatic brewer uses 63 g with 1 litre of water at medium-coarse grind, while a Kalita Wave uses 30 g with 500 g at medium grind and a 3:30–4:00 target. Those are roaster instructions, not Coffeedant brews; the separate general 1:17 advice is not an espresso yield. A household buying the dark Colombian blend for both batch coffee and small pour-over should record two grind settings and adjust each from the actual bag, rather than using the same setting because the coffee name is unchanged. Checked October 21, 2026. [SOURCE]
sourceTitle: Counter Culture Gradient device-specific brew panel
sourceNote: Official automatic-brewer and Kalita Wave recipes specify distinct dose, water, grind and Kalita time.

paragraph: The current Even Keel French-press panel contains an internal dose conflict: its summary says 50 g coffee to 800 g water (1:16), while step one says to measure 45 g, which would be about 1:17.8 for the same water. The published review previously treated the 50 g summary as a settled recipe. Start with a weighed dose and record which version you used; contact Counter Culture if exact replication matters. This inconsistency says nothing about the caffeine content of the brewed cup, which remains unmeasured here. Checked October 21, 2026. [SOURCE]
sourceTitle: Counter Culture Even Keel French-press recipe discrepancy
sourceNote: Current product panel summary says 50 g/800 g; its first instruction says 45 g/800 g.

paragraph: Eye of the Tiger's current roaster page gives different starts if espresso is only one use for the bag: its moka-pot guide lists 30 g coffee to 300 g water for a six-cup Bialetti, and its AeroPress guide lists 18 g to 200 g with a 50 g bloom and a two-minute stir-and-plunge point. Neither is a portafilter shot, so the page's separate 18 g to 46 g espresso example should not be transplanted to them. With a seasonally changing blend, note the bag date and device before comparing a later cup; these are Equator recipes, not Coffeedant extractions. Checked October 21, 2026. [SOURCE]
sourceTitle: Equator Eye of the Tiger multi-device brew guide
sourceNote: Current page distinguishes Barista Express espresso, six-cup Bialetti moka and AeroPress starts.

paragraph: Equator's current 1:15 guidance is device-specific, not just a single generic ratio: the drip start is 66 g to 1,000 g, the Fellow Clara press start is 45 g to 675 g with a one-minute stir and four-minute plunge, and the V60 start is 24 g to 360 g across a bloom and three pours. The press steps matter to a household comparing this medium-dark bag with an espresso-first blend: there is a reproducible immersion route here, while the listing still supplies no similarly precise portafilter target. Use whole beans if you need to move between devices. These are roaster recipes, not Coffeedant tasting or extraction results. Checked October 21, 2026. [SOURCE]
sourceNote: Current page gives 66 g/1,000 g drip, 45 g/675 g Clara, and 24 g/360 g V60 methods.
